prompt: Two robot grippers fold a photorealistic long-sleeve top on a real worktable: fold both sleeves across the chest, bring both hem corners toward the shoulders, release the garment, and return both grippers home. Cloth must preserve identity, wrinkle naturally, self-collide, remain supported by the table, and never pass through the grippers or table.

asset_contract.source: RoboDojo fold_clothes task geometry and success-condition reference only

reasons: static mesh rather than a cloth asset with simulation weights
cape/scarf topology rather than a Top_Long garment
no landmark map or self-collision evidence

required_assets: licensed long-sleeve garment mesh with landmark map

backend_options.blocked_reason: bimanual garment folding requires gripper-cloth coupling, cloth self-collision, landmark tracking, and a garment mesh; the current Taichi backend only supports drape/flag grids

benchmark_reference.name: RoboDojo fold_clothes
benchmark_reference.license_scope: MIT software license; benchmark assets and third-party data still require separate provenance review before ingestion
benchmark_reference.adaptation: success geometry and task structure only; no third-party binary asset is copied

notes: Contract-only case. It must remain fail-closed until two-way gripper contact, self-collision, garment landmarks, licensed realistic assets, and a native run are available. The benchmark task uses Top_Long garments and evaluates sleeve-to-opposite-chest, hem-to-shoulder, fold angle, open grippers, and return-to-home conditions. Laplace's unified local catalog was screened: its high-density SM_RedCloth_sim is useful as a drape/cape visual candidate but is rejected here because it is a static cape mesh without Top_Long landmarks, cloth weights, or self-collision evidence.
